title: Reject the unchanged copied-batch parallel parser
question: Does copied-batch parallel parsing beat the stronger strict serial parser?
summary: Retain the patch as rejected evidence; copied handoff and dispatch do not justify production integration.

workloads: Native plain-input ordered and allocation/shuffle complete Runs with four workers and matching 32-MiB limits.

validation.summary: Six measured jobs independently verify fields, unique IDs, groups, caps and cleanup; use the source narrative for the isolated prototype gates.

limitations: Small development cells and uncontrolled cache/background state do not establish general device, shape or tail performance.
Historical percentage gains are not additive; every comparison uses its own pinned baseline.
Suffix filtering is not a proven plain-input magic detector.
The result does not reject parallel parsing fused with useful initial computation.
exclusions: Upstream parser throughput and policy/dispatch costs do not establish isolated Chopper component speed.
reopen_when: Only a materially different integration with a named whole-job benefit question warrants reopening; preserve strict parser/admission contracts.
